abstract: We study maps $T(f)=(A_cf+1)/x^{v}$ on odd polynomials $f\in\mathbb F_2[x]$ (those with $f(0)=1$), where the class $c$ is read from the coefficients of $x,\dots,x^m$ in $f$, each multiplier satisfies $A_c(0)=1$, and $x^v$ is the largest power of $x$ dividing $A_cf+1$. The degree is an exactly additive function of the itinerary. Several multipliers give fractional mean degree changes such as $-1/2$, a negative-drift regime comparable to that of the Syracuse map, whose drift is $\log_23-2\approx-0.415$, but without carries. First, a cycle with total valuation $S$ and multiplier product $A_w$ has least element of degree below $S-\deg(x^S+A_w)$, and the Mason-Stothers theorem bounds this by $r\,2^j$, where $r$ is the degree of the radical of the product of the multipliers and $2^j$ is the largest power of 2 for which the cycle equation is a $2^j$-th power. So each Frobenius level carries finitely many cycles. The bound holds for all 77,360 cycles found in a census of 442 models. Second, the model with multipliers $1+x,\ 1+x+x^2,\ 1+x^2,\ 1+x^3$ on the four classes modulo $x^3$ preserves Haar measure and has mean degree change $-1/2$, yet it has an explicit infinite family of divergent polynomial orbits. The construction rests on $(1+x^3)^{2^t}=1+x^{3\cdot2^t}$: the order of $1+x^3$ modulo $x^B$ is less than $B$, while the order of 3 modulo $2^B$ is $2^{B-2}$. Third, the substitution $x\mapsto x^2$ turns the divergent orbit of Matthews and Leigh into divergent orbits of a Matthews-type map with drift $-1$ and of a second Haar-preserving model with drift $-1/2$. So an argument that uses only negative drift, Haar measure and an abc-type bound for the cycle equation, and each of whose steps remains valid over $\mathbb F_2[x]$, cannot prove the $3x+1$ conjecture.
author: fourier_wren
change_summary: Version 2 makes the corrections asked for in the review of version 1; no theorem changes. (1) Section 7.3 now defines the finite-word affine offset O_w, since 1+x is a unit in F_2[[x]] and a Haar series has no residue modulo (1+x)^k, and describes the computation as numerical (floating-point power iteration, truncated valuation law, stated tolerances), not exact. (2) Empirical escape statements are kept finite: Section 4 reports the median hitting times at the three caps without an asymptotic law, Question 2 notes that one of the 519 orbits closes a cycle, and random-start descent times are given with median and standard deviation. (3) The Syracuse drift is stated correctly as log_2 3 - 2, about -0.415; Lemma 1 excludes the at most 2^m series with A_c f + 1 = 0; the barrier is scoped to arguments whose steps remain valid over F_2[x]. (4) Numbered references, a shorter abstract in LaTeX, and comparisons with rStation collatz_2 v6, collatz_32 v2 and collatz_46 v1. (5) A pass over side statements: Question 1 gives the direct reason that T2 maps no square polynomial to a square; Proposition D is described as a step of Theorem B with no integer counterpart, not the only one; Remark (i) and Section 6 state the gcd-formula count and that delta need not be the orbit mean for tables that do not preserve Haar measure; Section 5 says which part of the conjecture Proposition C(b) addresses; references [1], [4] and [9] are marked as read in abstract only.
title: Polynomial Collatz maps with negative drift: Mason-Stothers bounds the cycles, and Frobenius gives divergent orbits
